name: Karuvalarcheri Agastheeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Thanjavur delta whose lingam is worshipped as Agastheeswarar, with the goddess Akilandesvari enshrined alongside. It draws childless couples who come to seek the blessing of children.
story: The goddess here is held to be self-manifested and is invoked as Karu Valarkkum Nayaki, the one who nurtures the growth of the unborn child.

name: Basuki Nath Mahadev Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple near the Indo-Nepal border in Madhubani district, founded by a local Maithil Brahmin family and reckoned to be more than a century and a half old. It is a regional pilgrimage point, busiest during Sawan jalabhisheka and Mahashivratri.

name: Jagannath Temple, Angul (Saila Srikhetra)
significance: Known as Saila Srikhetra, this Angul shrine houses the Jagannath triad and reproduces the ritual calendar of the great temple at Puri. Its Ratha Yatra and Snana Yatra make it a focal pilgrimage site for the surrounding district.

name: Pennadam Meikandar Temple
significance: An unusual shrine dedicated not to a god but to Meykandar, the Shaiva Siddhanta philosopher, and managed by the Thiruvaduthurai Adheenam. It was renovated and reconsecrated in June 2014.
story: The spot at Achuthakalappalarmedu in Pennadam is held to be the place where Meykandar was born.

name: Bhimambika Temple, Itagi
significance: A temple and mutt at Itagi in north Karnataka honouring Bhimambika Devi, also called Bheemavva, remembered as a Shiva Sharane. The seat has passed down one family line and is now in its eighth generation of custodians.

name: Uthanda Velayudhaswamy Temple, Uthiyur
deity: Murugan as Uthanda Velayudhaswamy, with Valli and Deivanai
significance: A ninth-century Murugan temple set on the Uthiyur hills in Tiruppur district, sung of as Uthimalai in Arunagirinathar's Thiruppugazh. It is a customary halt for pilgrims walking to Palani.

name: Shri Kamaksha Temple, Jaidevi
deity: Goddess Kamaksha (Kamakhya), with Mahunag Ji and Bala Tika Ji
significance: The shrine of Kamaksha at Jaidevi in Mandi district is the tutelary deity of the Suket royal house and a Himachali form of the goddess Kamakhya. It anchors the regional festival calendar, above all the Suket fair.
story: The goddess is said to have been carried from the old Suket capital at Pangana to the new palace when King Shyam Sen moved his seat, and the temple was raised for her at Jaidevi.

name: Shanaleshwara Swayambhu Temple
significance: A Shiva shrine near Rajpura built around a lingam held to be self-manifested, with a structure commissioned by the Maharaja of Patiala and a sadhu presence recorded from the fifteenth century. Hundreds of thousands of devotees converge on it at Maha Shivaratri.
story: A cowherd is said to have found the lingam after his cow kept letting down her milk at one spot; when the buried stone was struck it bled, and a sage nearby recognised it as divine.

name: Theeyathur Sahasralakshmeeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Theeyathur in Pudukkottai district whose presiding lingam is called Sahasralakshmeeswarar, with Periyanayaki as goddess and a large complement of subsidiary shrines.
story: Vishnu is said to have worshipped Shiva here with a thousand lotuses and, finding himself one short, offered his own eye; Shiva later gave darshan to Mahalakshmi when she made the same thousand-flower offering.

name: Engan Brahmapurisvarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple, also called Brahmeesvaram, in the village of Engan about 13 km from Tiruvarur. Its walled prakara holds several subsidiary shrines, including a prominent Murugan sannidhi reached from the southern entrance.

name: Pathala Ponniamman Temple
significance: An Amman temple in Kilpauk, Chennai, traced to the time of Chennappa Nayak and now administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department. It serves as the kuladeivam of roughly a lakh families across the city and its outskirts.
story: The image of the goddess is said to have come to light about thirty feet underground when a well was being dug at Purasawalkam, which is why she is called Pathala, of the netherworld.

name: Venugopalaswamy Temple, Ganapathy
significance: A Vaishnava temple in the Ganapathy quarter of Coimbatore, credited to a Mysore ruler of Yadava descent about a thousand years ago and renovated in 1764. It is now run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department, and the surrounding neighbourhood takes its name from the old Kottai Ganapathy shrine that stood before it.

name: Ramalingeswara Temple, Nandikandi
significance: An eleventh-century Shiva temple raised under the Kalyani Chalukyas, notable for its Bhumija shikhara over a star-shaped sanctum. It survives as a rare Deccan example of that form, though reported to be in poor repair.

name: Sankara Narayanasamy Temple, Sankarankovil
deity: Sankara Linga Swamy (Shiva) with Gomathi Amman, and Sankaranarayana, the joined form of Shiva and Vishnu
significance: The great temple that gives Sankarankovil its name, attributed to the Pandya king Ukkira Pandiyan in the tenth century and unusual in enshrining Shiva and Vishnu in a single joined form. Its Chithirai car festival and the Aadi Thabasu observance draw large crowds each year.

name: Kanak Bhawan
significance: One of Ayodhya's principal shrines, housing images of Rama and Sita in a palace-like building rebuilt in 1891 by Maharani Vrishabhan Kunwari and Maharaj Mahendra Pratap Singh. Its form deliberately echoes the palaces of Rajasthan and Bundelkhand.
story: Tradition holds that Kaikeyi gave this golden mansion to Rama and Sita as their private residence immediately after their marriage.

name: Hanuman Dandi Temple
significance: A shrine on the island of Beyt Dwarka that is rare in showing Hanuman together with his son Makaradhwaja, an unusual pairing given Hanuman's celibacy. Pilgrims to Dwarka commonly include it in their circuit.
story: Makaradhwaja is said to have been born of a drop of Hanuman's sweat swallowed by a fish, and father and son met in battle during the Ramayana.

name: Manokamna Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple in the Mithila country of north Bihar, roughly thirteen miles from Janakpur, whose name marks it as the place where wishes are granted. Its main gathering is the annual Sravani Mela.
story: Sita is said to have worshipped Girija Devi for twelve years and then to have been directed to this spot, where prayers are fulfilled.
